parameters.content:
## Bonus B3 — Read a Google Doc (Reference, live)

No Google node, no OAuth, no API key. A published Google Doc can be fetched as plain text by URL — so "connecting to Google Docs" is just the **HTTP Request** node you already know from Ex 00 and Ex 07.

```
Doc ID → Fetch Doc (HTTP, export?format=txt) → Extract Action Items (LLM) → Result
```

**Read-only.** This reads a published doc; it cannot write back. Writing needs the real Google Docs node + a Service Account (see the setup note). For getting document text *into* a workflow, this is the simplest path that exists.

## To run this live (one-time, ~2 min)

1. Open a Google Doc (or make one — paste in `sample-doc.txt` from this folder).
2. **Share → General access → Anyone with the link → Viewer.** (Or File → Share → Publish to web.)
3. Copy the doc ID from the URL: `docs.google.com/document/d/`**`THIS_PART`**`/edit`.
4. Paste it into **Set Input → `doc_id`** and run.

**If you get HTML back instead of your text:** the doc isn't link-shared yet — Google returned a sign-in page. Fix the sharing setting.

### The three ways to reach Google from n8n
- **Export URL (this exercise)** — zero credentials, read-only. Best for getting text in.
- **Service Account** — make a Google Cloud service account, paste its JSON key into an n8n Google credential, then *share the doc with the service-account email*. No browser/consent dance. Use this when you need to WRITE.
- **OAuth2** — full consent-screen flow with a redirect to `http://localhost:5678/rest/oauth2-credential/callback`. Most powerful, most setup. Overkill for class.

**No doc to publish?** Import `B3-c-reference-offline.workflow.json` instead — it runs with no Google setup at all.
